column11: derived and found to be nil: NVS's filed expense lines already leave less than the 31.44% of revenue it turned into free cash over 2023 to 2025, so there is nothing left to charge. Restated before interest: NVS paid $2,587mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 1.72% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so adding it back only widens a gap the filed lines already leave, and the charge stays nil. Checked at replacement capex: no plant depreciation on file for every year, and no amortisation line to take it out of the combined figure, so the charge stands. Checked without one-off cash: deal payments are booked under investing, so free cash flow never carried them, and no settlement or transition tax is stated for the window, so the charge stands. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 30.05% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2023 to 2025 supports 37.20%, so the charge rebuilds at -7.15%. It was held at nil, but NVS books $3,197mm of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside its cost lines in FY2025 (0001114448-26-000004), 5.86% of revenue, so the charge stops at that floor: -5.86%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 NVS's cash flow statement shows receivables up $3,559mm, inventories up $737mm, payables up $101mm, a working capital build of $4,195mm, 2.79% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge was held at the amortisation floor, -5.86% where the filed figures rebuild it at -7.15%, and stays there. Struck on total revenue: Novartis's filed cost lines sit against net sales of USD 54,532mm and other revenues of USD 2,142mm together (FY2025 20-F 0001114448-26-000004, Note 4), and the income statement shows other revenues above cost of goods sold with no cost of their own, so each ratio is scaled by 54,532 over 56,674 and charged on every revenue the model carries. The book's costs are the filed ones either way; this shares them across the revenue that earned them. Rebuilt on the book's own ratios on 0.3269 of the revenue they are struck on, against 0.3911 the filings leave as cash over 2023 to 2025 (free cash flow before interest, at replacement capex, without one-off cash and without working capital build), so the charge is -5.8626%.

column11: already approved, and this is the confirmatory study. VANRAFIA is indicated to reduce proteinuria in adults with primary IgAN at risk of rapid disease progression, 'generally a urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR) >= 1.5 g/g', under accelerated approval contingent on a confirmatory trial (NDA 219208, openFDA drug/label, effective 2026-06-12, section 1). ALIGN (NCT04573478, 404 adults with proteinuria of at least 1.0 g/day on a RAS inhibitor) is that trial. Its double-blind section is complete and published: Heerspink HJL et al., Lancet 2026;407(10546):2387-2401, doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(26)00960-8, eGFR change at week 136 of -7.5 against -9.9 mL/min/1.73m2 on placebo, a difference of 2.4 (95% CI -0.1 to 4.8; p=0.057), total eGFR slope difference 1.4 a year. The registry's 2028-04-14 date is the end of the open-label extension and substudy, whose primary outcomes are adverse event counts
